newsitem.title: FRANCE: ETA's bloody "French commando" tried in France.
newsitem.headline: ETA's bloody "French commando" tried in France.

text.p: Six French Basques went on trial in a Paris assize court on Monday, suspected of killing 37 people in Spain as members of ETA's notorious "roving French commando", one of the Basque guerrilla organisation's bloodiest groups.
The men, one of whom had joined a monastery before being arrested, face multiple charges of murder and conspiracy to terrorism.

The squad made raids into Spain in 1978-1989 and is held responsible for killing 10 senior Spanish army and navy officers, two magistrates, a businessman who refused to pay ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) "revolutionary taxes" and several passers-by.
In its bloodiest attack, it bombed a Civil Guard barracks in Saragossa in 1987, killing 11 people, including children, and wounding 78.
ETA has killed some 800 people in its three-decade-old campaign for a Basque state independent from Madrid.

ETA's only squad made up of non-Spaniards, the "French commando" was believed to have been under direct control of the group's top leaders, Domingo "Txomin" Iturbe Abasolo in 1978-81, then Juan Lorenzo "Txikierdi" Lasa Michelena until 1989.

The elusive squad was smashed after its presumed leader, Henri Parrot, was arrested in 1990 as he drove a car loaded with 323 kilos of explosives into Seville which was then preparing to host the 1992 World Fair.
Spanish police believe the explosives were intended to blow up the city's police headquarters.
Parot is being held in Spain and the defendants, who include his 46-year-old brother Jean, asked the Paris court to summon him as a witness. The presiding judge made no decision on the request.
The other defendants are Frederic Haramboure, 43, Jacques Esnal, 46, Jean-Pierre Erremundeguy, 42, Jean-Vincent Garcia, 42, and monk Philippe Saez, 38.
A seventh suspected member of the group, 52-year-old Jose Arrieta Zubimendi, is on the run and being tried in absentia as an accomplice to murder.

Unlike other French assize courts, the Paris court is made up of magistrates and has no popular jury in order to avoid intimidation of jury members. The trial is expected to last until the end of the month.
